key_patterns: aws-cdk-lib 2.266.0 API confirmed by reading node_modules type defs: cloudfront.Function with FunctionCode.fromInline(string) and optional runtime (FunctionRuntime.JS_2_0; default JS_1_0). FunctionEventType.VIEWER_REQUEST exists. A behavior takes functionAssociations?: [{ function, eventType }]. cloudfront.OriginRequestPolicy ctor takes { headerBehavior, cookieBehavior, queryStringBehavior }. OriginRequestHeaderBehavior.allowList(...headers) forwards ONLY the listed headers; CloudFront-Viewer-Country and CloudFront-Viewer-City are CloudFront-generated headers that CloudFront ADDS when the policy allow-lists them (confirmed against AWS docs adding-cloudfront-headers). OriginRequestQueryStringBehavior.all() forwards all query strings. OriginRequestCookieBehavior.none(). Host is ALWAYS auto-included by CloudFront as the ORIGIN host and must NOT be in the allowList (the managed ALL_VIEWER_EXCEPT_HOST_HEADER excludes Host for exactly this Function-URL-origin reason). The stack already imports `cloudfront` (aws-cdk-lib/aws-cloudfront) and `origins` (aws-cdk-lib/aws-cloudfront-origins).

headers_redirect_consumes: From apps/redirect/src/main.ts, the request headers the redirect path reads (Fastify lowercases header names): x-forwarded-host (primary host resolution, set by the new CloudFront Function), host (fallback host resolution), user-agent (device/browser/os parsing + bot detection), cloudfront-viewer-country (country routing rules + click_events.country), cloudfront-viewer-city (click_events.city), accept-language (language routing), referer (referrerHost parse + QR detection). It also uses the URL query string: request.url query part (UTM/forwardQuery in buildDestination) and request.query.k (password unlock token). Therefore the OriginRequestPolicy allowList must contain: user-agent, referer, accept-language, x-forwarded-host, CloudFront-Viewer-Country, CloudFront-Viewer-City; and queryString behavior must be all(). Host is intentionally EXCLUDED.
